reason: The cited evidence (E1-E4) confirms that MgTiZn alloys form intermetallics (Ti2Zn, Mg21Zn25) and a TiO2-rich passivating film that provides good corrosion resistance, but it provides no data on thermal exposure effects, precipitate evolution kinetics, or the temperature-dependent mechanistic pathway proposed. The key premises about discontinuous precipitation, temperature-specific microstructural outcomes, and in-situ correlation are entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: MgTiZn alloys can be produced in a metastable solid-solution state via mechanical alloying and rapid consolidation
Thermal exposure triggers a discontinuous precipitation reaction forming nanoscale intermetallics
At ~350°C, fine homogeneous precipitates promote a continuous TiO2-rich passivating film, maintaining/enhancing corrosion and oxidation resistance
At ~500°C, precipitate coarsening and intergranular segregation disrupt the protective film, degrading resistance
In-situ TEM and time-resolved XPS can directly correlate precipitate evolution with oxide layer changes
